projects.title: The Courtyards at Fullerton
projects.type: Residential over commercial retail and parking
projects.summary: The Courtyards at Fullerton transforms a complex infill site into a four-story podium community that integrates housing, commercial uses, parking, and shared open space within a cohesive urban development.
body: The 165,884 SF project includes 95 one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences, with 10% designated as affordable housing and a residential density of approximately 50 units per acre. Housing is organized above commercial space and a parking garage, with approximately 4,000 SF of ground-floor lease office and retail/service uses. Public and private open spaces are distributed throughout the development, including landscaped gathering areas, a community room, children’s play area, dog park, and resident courtyards. The architecture responds to the irregular site through connected building masses and an urban infill character, while the entitlement process included rezoning to R5/Mixed-Use, a lot-line merger, conditional use permit, and CEQA negative declaration study.

projects.title: Linden Point
projects.type: Live-work townhomes and stacked flats over retail
projects.summary: Linden Point combines housing, work-live units, and neighborhood-serving commercial space within a contemporary infill development designed to support both living and working on one site.
body: Located in West Sacramento, the project includes 15 residences—six three-level work-live townhomes and nine stacked flats—along with commercial retail and service uses, with 10% of the housing designated as affordable. Each work-live unit provides an independently accessed commercial space at street level, living space on the second floor, and two bedrooms on the third, while the stacked flats average approximately 1,400 SF and are organized within a low-rise four-story building over retail. Metal cladding, cement plaster, projecting volumes, and angular parapets create a varied contemporary façade, while outdoor gathering areas, EV charging, and photovoltaic canopies over parking extend the project’s emphasis on shared space and energy-conscious design.

projects.title: 1012 J Street
projects.type: Retail and lobby at street level, residential above
projects.summary: 1012 J Street gives new life to an existing downtown Sacramento building through adaptive reuse, introducing residential living above active commercial space just two blocks from the State Capitol.
body: The 10,524 SF renovation converts a former office building historically occupied by a law school and library into a mixed-use development with commercial uses at the basement and first floor and four one-bedroom residences above. Approximately 3,000 SF of street-level retail is paired with a dedicated lobby providing stair and elevator access to the residential floor and basement, while the four residences range from approximately 560 to 650 SF. Because of its downtown location, the project is exempt from on-site parking requirements. A major façade renovation introduces brick veneer, black metal fenestration, and canopies, while accessibility, circulation, rooftop systems, and the existing structure are upgraded to support the new program.

projects.title: Chino Hills Residence
projects.summary: This custom Chino Hills residence combines refined Mediterranean architecture with expansive living spaces, resort-style amenities, and seamless indoor-outdoor connections.
body: The approximately 10,150 SF estate includes six bedrooms and ten bathrooms, with a formal interior sequence defined by double-height spaces, dual staircases, an elevator, fireplaces, detailed millwork, stone flooring, and ornate classical detailing. Stucco walls, stone accents, clay tile roofs, arched openings, wrought-iron elements, and French doors establish a cohesive Mediterranean material palette throughout. The main living spaces open toward terraces, balconies, and a landscaped rear courtyard with a pool, spa, outdoor kitchen, multiple seating areas, and a circular pavilion, creating a strong connection between the home's interiors and its hillside setting.

projects.title: Bellflower Residences

videos.caption: Fly-through — the shared drive and motor court.

projects.summary: Bellflower Residences brings eight two-story homes together in a cohesive residential development that blends Mediterranean-inspired character with a comfortable suburban scale.
body: The homes are organized as individual residences with private driveways and two-car garages, creating a clear sense of ownership while maintaining a unified streetscape. Stucco walls, warm clay tile roofs, stone veneer accents, and modest arched openings establish the architectural language, while varied rooflines, recessed entries, balconies, and projecting garage volumes give each home depth and distinction. Landscaping between the residences softens the street edge and reinforces the neighborhood character, resulting in a compact development that feels residential, approachable, and visually consistent without becoming repetitive.

projects.title: Irvine Residence Interior
projects.summary: A gut renovation of a tower condominium, opened up to the glass so the city view is the first thing you see from the entry and the last thing from the kitchen.
body: The original plan boxed the living space away from the windows. The renovation removes those walls, drops a long island where a partition used to be, and lines the kitchen up so the view runs uninterrupted from the front door to the far glass.

The palette is deliberately quiet — white lacquer, book-matched quartz, warm brass — so the changing light off the windows carries the room. A glass-walled study borrows that light without giving up acoustic separation.
Every surface, fixture and lighting position was drawn; the contractor built from a full interior set.

projects.title: Sharif Jewelers — Roseville

videos.caption: The flagship showroom and the leased office/retail building.

videosEnd.caption: Cars and pedestrians arriving at the flagship.

projects.summary: Sharif & Co. transforms six generations of family craftsmanship into a flagship architectural identity inspired by the materiality, precision, and presentation of fine jewelry.
body: Located in Roseville near the Galleria and surrounding retail district, the development consists of a 5,952 SF flagship jewelry showroom, including its mezzanine, and a separate 1,850 SF medical office building. The showroom is conceived as a jewel box holding precious gems, with three sculptural buttresses representing the Sharif family’s past, present, and future. Metal composite cladding references the role of metal in goldsmithing, while expansive glazing creates transparency and allows natural light to animate both the façade and jewelry displays. Inside, the showroom is envisioned with a museum-like quality that places the jewelry at the center of the experience, while the building’s distinctive form and scale establish a recognizable presence within Roseville.

projects.title: Sharif Jewelers — Elk Grove
projects.summary: Sharif Jewelers transforms an existing commercial interior in Elk Grove into a refined jewelry showroom organized around elegant circulation, layered lighting, and a warm contemporary material palette.
body: The approximately 4,994 SF tenant improvement combines retail display areas with a vault, offices, lounge, break room, and accessory support spaces. Curved display counters and a large circular ceiling feature establish a clear focal point within the showroom, while dark wood millwork, polished stone flooring, glass display cases, and warm metallic accents create a sophisticated setting for the jewelry. A combination of recessed, accent, and decorative lighting highlights merchandise and defines key areas throughout the space, while expansive glazing brings natural light into the showroom. The project also includes new interior partitions, reflected ceiling and lighting improvements, selective HVAC modifications, electrical adjustments, and accessibility upgrades to the primary entrance, circulation route, and restrooms.

projects.title: The Diamond Ring Company
projects.summary: The Diamond Ring Company transforms a 2,310 SF mall tenant space into a refined jewelry showroom centered on visibility, elegance, and a strong luxury retail identity.
body: Located at Westfield Valley Fair in San Jose, the tenant improvement introduces a new storefront and a complete interior refresh while retaining portions of the existing ceiling structure. The design is organized around illuminated glass display cases, dark wood cabinetry, polished flooring, and a restrained black, white, and champagne-gold palette that gives the showroom a sophisticated, gallery-like character. A geometric gold feature wall and coordinated storefront surround reinforce the brand at key focal points, while layered lighting, mirrored elements, and crystal chandeliers add depth and brightness throughout the space. The project also includes updated lighting, modified HVAC distribution, raised soffits, new floor finishes, and new store fixtures, resulting in a cohesive retail environment designed to showcase the jewelry as the primary visual focus.

projects.title: J & Huss Custom Jewelry
projects.summary: J & Huss Custom Jewelry transforms a compact mall tenant space into a refined, contemporary showroom that uses transparency, lighting, and carefully detailed displays to give the brand a stronger retail presence.
body: Located at Eastridge Mall in San Jose, the approximately 789 SF tenant improvement introduces a new storefront, updated lighting, floor finishes, and custom jewelry fixtures within the existing shell. The design pairs a white brick façade with black metal framing and expansive glazing to create a crisp, highly visible storefront, while the interior uses a restrained palette of warm neutrals, dark accents, illuminated wall displays, and glass showcases to keep the jewelry as the primary focus. Raised soffits and layered lighting help define key display and service areas, while selective HVAC modifications and the reuse of the existing ceiling allow the renovation to work efficiently within the existing building conditions.

projects.title: Gold & Diamond
projects.summary: Gold & Diamond transforms a compact retail footprint into a bright, contemporary jewelry showroom where clean architectural lines, refined materials, and layered lighting create an elevated setting for merchandise display.
body: The approximately 869 SF tenant improvement is organized around a 685 SF retail showroom supported by dedicated storage/utility and restroom spaces. The renovation includes a completely redesigned storefront, new non-bearing partitions, ceilings and soffits, lighting, floor finishes, HVAC distribution, and custom store fixtures. A crisp palette of white stone and marble-inspired surfaces, black metal detailing, polished flooring, and expansive glazing gives the storefront a strong presence within the surrounding retail environment. Inside, illuminated glass showcases line the perimeter and define clear circulation through the showroom, while integrated display lighting and a sculptural central fixture create focal points throughout the space. The result is a compact but polished retail environment designed to maximize product visibility while giving Gold & Diamond a distinct, sophisticated identity.

projects.title: Huntington Beach Medical Offices
projects.type: Free-standing medical and professional office building
projects.summary: Huntington Beach Medical Offices creates a contemporary three-tenant healthcare destination designed around visibility, accessibility, and a welcoming patient experience.
body: Located along Brookhurst Street, the project develops the 35,000 SF site with approximately 7,600 SF of medical office space organized into three tenant suites. The architecture breaks down the building mass through varied rooflines, contrasting façade materials, and clearly defined storefront entries, giving each practice an individual identity while maintaining a cohesive overall design. Expansive glazing brings natural light into the tenant spaces, while integrated parking, landscaping, and accessible circulation create a functional and approachable environment for patients, staff, and visitors.

projects.title: Power Market Gas Station
projects.summary: Power Market in Woodland establishes a flood-resilient roadside prototype that brings fueling, convenience retail, food service, car wash, and EV charging together within one coordinated development.
body: Located on a corner site adjacent to the Interstate 5 southbound ramp, the project is anchored by an approximately 4,200 SF Power Market convenience store incorporating a full-size Papa Sal’s Deli. The fueling canopy provides six pumps and twelve gasoline and diesel dispensers, while the automatic touch-free car wash incorporates filtration and water-reuse technology to reduce water consumption. Level 3 DC fast charging expands the site’s range of vehicle services. Because the property lies within a flood zone, the development was designed for a 200-year flood event, requiring the c-store to be elevated using retaining walls and coordinated grading. Layered massing, storefront glazing, stone, plaster, metal, aluminum, and warm accent materials establish a contemporary architectural language that was developed as a prototype for future H&S Energy convenience-store projects.

projects.title: Union City Power Market
projects.summary: Union City Power Market reimagines the neighborhood service station as a contemporary, pedestrian-conscious retail destination that integrates architecture, circulation, and public transit access.
body: The redevelopment replaces the existing convenience store and fueling canopy with a new 2,375 SF Power Market and an expanded 2,875 SF canopy on the approximately 0.5-acre site. The building is composed through a series of articulated volumes, including a prominent stone-clad entry tower, lower storefront elements, and contrasting vertical masses that create a strong identity along Alvarado-Niles Road. Architectural stone, smooth plaster, metal cladding, wood-toned accents, aluminum canopies, and expansive glazing establish a cohesive contemporary material palette across the site. The store is positioned to maintain efficient vehicular circulation while creating safer pedestrian connections to the adjacent transportation center, with accessible parking and routes designed to minimize conflicts with vehicle traffic. Landscaped buffers, consolidated site access, and integrated service elements further strengthen the relationship between the development, surrounding streets, and public realm.

projects.title: Montclair Chevron Gas Station
projects.summary: Montclair Chevron repositions an existing service station as a contemporary automotive and retail destination, integrating fueling, convenience retail, and car wash functions within a compact and highly coordinated site.
body: Located along Central Avenue, the redevelopment introduces a new approximately 1,750 SF ExtraMile convenience store, a 495 SF automatic car wash, supporting equipment spaces, and an updated Chevron fueling environment. The architecture combines brick masonry, smooth stucco, metal detailing, broad storefront glazing, and articulated parapet elements to create a cohesive identity across the store and car wash. A taller central entry volume establishes a clear focal point, while lower horizontal masses and canopies help organize the building at a pedestrian scale. Site planning carefully coordinates fueling, parking, car wash circulation, service access, and landscaped edges within the constrained 0.49-acre property, creating an efficient customer experience while giving the station a stronger architectural presence along the street.

projects.title: Metro Fusion
projects.type: In-line retail tenant improvement and storefront
projects.summary: Metro Fusion turns a visibility-constrained retail space into a stronger public-facing storefront by extending the store’s architectural identity beyond the limits of the tenant space.
body: The approximately 4,000 SF retail store is positioned beneath a second-level mezzanine, where limited vertical clearance created challenges for storefront visibility and branding. Rather than allowing the low mezzanine condition to define the store, the design uses the surrounding structure as an extension of the storefront, carrying finishes and architectural elements beyond the tenant boundary and into the public area. This strategy increases the store’s visual presence and creates a more identifiable retail frontage despite the constrained existing condition.

projects.title: West Valley Water Treatment Plant
projects.summary: West Valley Water Treatment Plant expands critical treatment infrastructure while creating a dedicated operations environment that brings technical, administrative, and employee spaces together within one cohesive facility.
body: Owned by West Valley Water District, the project combines a 7,696 SF filtration building with a 2,685 SF operations building designed to support both plant processes and day-to-day staff functions. The pre-engineered metal filtration building provides large clear-span spaces and oversized roll-up doors for equipment access and maintenance, while the operations building houses a laboratory, SCADA and PLC rooms, offices, a breakroom with kitchen, employee facilities, and an education and training center. Contrasting metal cladding, stucco volumes, stone accents, exposed structural elements, and generous glazing distinguish the public-facing operations spaces from the more utilitarian treatment areas, creating a unified civic-industrial campus that supports both infrastructure and the people who operate it.

projects.title: Solano Water Treatment Plant
projects.summary: Solano Water Treatment Plant combines a highly technical one-MGD treatment program with a hybrid building system designed around UC Davis standards, process flow, future expansion, and long-term operational efficiency.
body: Owned by UC Davis and located just off campus, the facility accommodates filtration equipment, pumps, electrical systems, laboratory and control spaces, and the clear-span service areas required for plant operations and maintenance. The building uses concrete masonry up to approximately 8'-8" with a prefabricated metal structure above, creating a durable base around equipment and circulation while giving the facility greater architectural articulation than a conventional all-metal industrial building. Large service openings support equipment access, while a separate canopy shelters tanks and less-sensitive process equipment, reducing enclosed building area and construction cost. The design also allows for future expansion as treatment capacity increases while maintaining the operational requirements and design standards established by UC Davis.

projects.title: Ontario Water Treatment Plant — Well 37 & 39
projects.summary: Ontario Wells 37 & 39 Water Treatment Plant pairs highly technical water infrastructure with a durable, straightforward architectural expression designed around long-term operation and maintenance.
body: The approximately 1,992 SF CMU facility houses treatment equipment and chemical systems alongside an office, storage area, generator room, and electrical room. Its simple gabled form and metal roof create a compact, utilitarian building envelope, while tan masonry and horizontal textured CMU bands give the exterior depth and a cohesive civic-industrial character. Large service openings and direct connections to exterior tanks, piping, valves, and treatment equipment support efficient access for daily operations and maintenance, allowing the architecture and process infrastructure to function as an integrated system.

projects.title: Ontario Water Treatment Plant 925
projects.summary: Ontario 925 Water Treatment Plant combines robust utility infrastructure with a straightforward architectural expression designed around long-term operation, maintenance, and equipment access.
body: The approximately 9,199 SF facility is constructed as a concrete masonry building with a single-ply roof system and is organized to support the pumping, control, instrumentation, and chemical treatment systems serving Reservoir 925. Program spaces include a pump room, control room, chemical storage and generation area, generator enclosure, electrical room, and associated support spaces. Large roll-up doors and generous service clearances provide direct access for equipment installation and maintenance, while the exterior uses brick masonry, concrete accents, and carefully proportioned openings to give the highly technical facility a durable and cohesive civic-industrial character.
